issues.title: Handshake Context for supplemental authentication is not defined
issues.author: tireddy2
issues.body:
The draft describes transcript construction for supplemental authentication, but it does not explicitly define this in terms of the Handshake Context defined in Section 4.4 of TLS 1.3. 

The draft should explicitly define the Handshake Context used for supplemental authentication sequences.

a) The Handshake Context will differ between the client and the server, consistent with the Table in Section 4.4.
b) The Handshake Context should include the CertificateRequest message that carries the supplemental_certificate_requests extension.

Previously transmitted supplemental authentication messages would become part of the evolving Handshake Context, so that each subsequent CertificateVerify and Finished computation includes them.

Apart from the definition of the Handshake Context, the construction of CertificateVerify and Finished should follow the same rules defined in Section 4.4 of TLS 1.3.

issues.title: Base key for supplemental Finished not specified
issues.author: tireddy2
issues.body: Since supplemental authentication occurs after the handshake, Base Key should be [sender]_application_traffic_secret_N.

issues.title: Interaction with KeyUpdate, EKU, and post-handshake client authentication
issues.author: tireddy2
issues.body: We should clarify whether KeyUpdate, EKU, and post-handshake client authentication messages can interleave with supplemental authentication sequences, and whether any ordering restrictions are required.

issues.title: Compatibility with QUIC post-handshake restrictions
issues.author: tireddy2
issues.body:
RFC 9001 states that servers MUST NOT use post-handshake client authentication and specifically:

servers MUST NOT send post-handshake TLS CertificateRequest messages, and clients MUST treat receipt of such messages as a connection error of type PROTOCOL_VIOLATION.

Since this draft introduces additional Certificate, CertificateVerify, and Finished authentication sequences after the handshake, it is unclear how this mechanism would operate over QUIC without violating the QUIC-TLS restriction.

issues.title: Clarity on cross-flight of supplemental authentication messages
issues.author: tireddy2

issues.title: application data be exchanged relative to supplemental authentication
issues.author: tireddy2
issues.body: Whether application data can be sent after each supplemental authentication sequence, or only after all supplemental authentication has completed ?

issues.title: Identities for subsequent authentication
issues.author: tireddy2
issues.body:
whether multiple supplemental authentication sequences may represent the same identity using different certificate chains or present alternative identities ?

It looks like the draft is an alternative mechanism for RFC9261.

issues.title: identity to provide for supplemental authentication
issues.author: tireddy2
issues.body: It is not clear how a responding endpoint determines which identity or certificate chain to present, especially when the peers are not managed by the same administrative entity.  It looks the proposed draft will only work in deployments where both the peers are managed by the same entity.

issues.title: Impact of supplemental authentication on the TLS key schedule
issues.author: tireddy2
issues.body: It does not describe the impact of these post-handshake supplemental authentication messages on the TLS key schedule.
